title: Author-reported resource tradeoff in Classiq block-encoding synthesis
evidence_type: author-reported compilation result; not independently executed or reproduced in this review
execution_level: classical synthesis of logical quantum circuits; not a physical-QPU experiment

source.title: Design and synthesis of scalable quantum programs
source.publication_status_checked: arXiv preprint; a peer-reviewed publication for this benchmark paper was not identified in this review

software.note: This is the paper's software version, not the current Classiq SDK version at the review cutoff.

model.operation: block encoding of matrix A defined in equation (1)
model.N_definition: The matrix A has dimensions 2^N by 2^N; N specifies the matrix-size exponent, not the total number of circuit qubits.
model.scope_note: These two points describe the block-encoding construction in Figure 3; they are not the full polynomial-QSVT comparison in Figure 4.

metrics.maximum_width_qubits: Upper bound imposed on the synthesized circuit width, not the resulting width.
metrics.actual_width_qubits: Author-reported number of circuit qubits in the chosen implementation, including auxiliaries.
metrics.cx_count: Author-reported logical CX gate count. The paper's comparison uses one-qubit and CX gate operations.

interpretation_limits: The width constraint changes which implementation is selected; the two constraints are not actual widths.
Two reported points do not establish a complete Pareto frontier or a globally optimal circuit.
These values are not a current-version comparison against Qiskit or CUDA-Q.
Logical gate counts do not establish physical execution time, hardware fidelity, or quantum computational advantage.
